questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I am very interested in the Icelandic language. I have previously been there to learn it, and I wanted to get better at it. I have also worked for a professor at the University of Iceland (remotely from Denmark). I could take a course in Old Norse literature which I found fascinating and relevant to my education, even though I mainly study historical linguistics.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
I think the exchange itself was very good - it was not too difficult to get everyting in order and to move to Iceland. I learned so much from being there as well. My only complaint was that I wasn't allowed to choose language courses. I really wanted to learn more Icelandic and Old Norse, but I could only do that in my spare time, so I really didn't make that much progress with regards to that.

I was however very lonely and I had a hard time making friends, and I lost contact with my friends back home. Because I am autistic, I really struggle with these things, and it was hard to make it through the semester while being so lonely, but that is my own problem, and it hopefully won't be a problem for most other exchange students.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy, I just had to show up at the help desk and they sorted everything out in about 15 minutes or so. After a couple of hours, I had access to Canvas and such.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They gave me useful information at the help desk, and there were many introductory meetings and social events for exchange students the first week. Nothing to complain about at all.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were studio flats and a hall of residence. I applied for both, and I was given a flat.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I had my own little kitchen in my flat. I don't know what it was like in the other types of student housing.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I was mostly satisfied, but they were renovating my building while I lived there, so it was noisy, and they turned off the heat and warm water every now and then. The only rooms that come with furniture are the ones in the hall of residence, but it is possible to rent a chair and a bed from the student housing office. You can't really bring your own furniture to Iceland, so it helps a little.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I believe that originally had to select my courses back in April or May in some online portal for upcoming exchange students. When I showed up in August, I just had to talk to the people at the help desk and show them my passport. It was very easy really.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: The people at the help desk could answer questions, and we were given plenty of information the first week. I had some questions during the initial application back in April that I could get answered because they didn't reply to my emails, but it all worked out in the end.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was registered for the courses that I had selected. Of course, I would have preferred to have taken some langugage courses, but i wasn't allowed to do that by UCPH.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I'm not sure I have any specific advice. It wasn't that difficult, and while it may be confusing during the process, it will most certainly work out in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought they were similar in difficulty to the ones at UCPH. There was one 'Languages and Culture' that was a good deal more on the easy side.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The main difference is that there are many more assignments throughout the semester and that the final exams are not quite as intense. I think this is a much, much nicer way of doing things!

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Old Norse-Icelandic Literary Corpus - Overview and Main Questions: An introduction to Old Norse literature and its historical context.

Vocabulary Acquisition - Research and Theory: An introduction to research into vocabulary acquistion in mainly English, but to a lesser extent also other languages.

Languages and Culture I: A broad course covering the social aspects of many languages, with a few classes dedicated to each (Arabic, Latin, indigenous languages, English et cetera).

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The courses on Old Norse literature and vocabulary acquisition were really good, the teachers were serious, and I found the information that I learned useful. 'Languages and Culture I' was too unsfocused and covered too many different things, and I don't think it was that interesting or useful.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I was undergoing medical examinations in Denmark before I left for Iceland. This started half a year before I went to Iceland, but it dragged out, and I had to go to Denmark no less than three times. Those plane tickes cost quite a bit of money, and they are included in the 'other fees' (along with all the stuf I had to buy for my flat, since I couldn't bring everything with me on the plane). It was also very expensive to send all the stuff I had bought back to Denmark. I had to send several packages, and I had to pay toll and VAT for each of them.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The prices were similar to those in Denmark. I wasn't really that surprised.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I didn't have the energy to seek out these things while in Iceland, so I can't comment much on it.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There was a gym on campus, but apart from that I am not really sure.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Again, I didn't participate in any, so I can't comment on it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: It is definitely important to explore the countryside outside of Reykjavik. I don't have a drivers licence, so I had to go on bus trips. They university also organises bus trips to historical sites. The ones organised by the university are much better than those offered by tourist companies!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Danish and Icelandic culture are very similar to each other, so it was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I didn't find it difficult at all.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the Icelandic language, and I wish I had had more time to study it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
While the nature is very exotic in Iceland, the rest of Iceland feels very much like Denmark, so don't worry about cultural issues, it is easy to fit in in Iceland. It is easy to use English in Reykjavik, and many people even speak Danish or Swedish.

The process of applying to go on exchange seems very confusing while you are going through it, but it will work out in the end. Once you show up at the university before the semester, it is very simple from there.

It is only possible to bring so many things with you on the plane, so be prepared to spend a good deal of money when you arrive, especially if you get an empty flat like I did.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Not really, I don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I learned so much from being completely on my own in another country. I got a lot better at dealing with unforseen problems while also managing my studies. It is a very enriching experience that university students shouldn't miss out on!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: My greatest challenge was the loneliness and isolation, because I had a hard time making friends and keeping in touch with my friends in Denmark. I think that many exhange students may face this problem, but is much worse for someone with autism. But I don't think it should deter you from going on exchange!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
